title: Sense of security among nurses in acute care
summary:
This study focuses on the sense of security experienced by nurses working in German university hospitals. Nurses play a vital role in patient safety but often face high workloads, stress, and challenging situations, which can affect how safe they feel at work.
We aim to better understand how nurses define and experience security or insecurity in their daily practice, how they cope with such situations, and what support they consider helpful. To do so, we will conduct confidential interviews with nurses who have worked in direct patient care for at least six months. The findings will help to build a comprehensive understanding of nurses’ sense of security and guide measures to improve working conditions in hospitals.
conditions: Work-related stress and nurses’ sense of security in acute hospital care (psychosocial and organizational factors, workload, burnout risks)

interventions.name: Nurses working in direct patient care at four German university hospitals will participate in a single problem-centered interview (approx. 60 minutes) about their subjective sense of security at work.
